citeAs: Li, Kunchang, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, and Yu Qiao (2024). MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark.
creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao (Shanghai AI Laboratory)
description: MVBench is a comprehensive multi-modal video understanding benchmark for evaluating the temporal understanding capabilities of multi-modal large language models. It covers 20 challenging temporal video tasks and is built by automatically converting annotations from 11 public video benchmarks into multiple-choice question-answer pairs.
name: MVBench
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The benchmark uses an automatic annotation paradigm to generate multiple-choice QA from public video annotations. ChatGPT is used to generate questions for some tasks based on task definitions, answer candidates are built either from templates grounded in source annotations or via LLM-based generation, then 3 to 5 options are sampled and shuffled, and option lengths are normalized to reduce answer leakage.
rai:dataCollection: The benchmark is constructed by selecting videos from 11 existing public video datasets and automatically converting their open-sourced annotations into multiple-choice question-answer pairs guided by temporal task definitions. The authors filter videos for diversity, temporal sensitivity, and question difficulty, and ultimately produce 200 QA pairs for each of 20 temporal understanding tasks.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The authors exclude videos or questions that do not meet filtering criteria, such as short clips with negligible motion, extremely long videos with overly complicated contexts, CLEVRER questions requiring too many conditions, and Perception Test state-change questions that require audio.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of videos and public annotations from 11 source benchmarks: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that MVBench has a minimal source gap with some instruction-tuning data, specifically that CLEVRER in the instruction data has similar questions to MVBench tasks and Action Antonym videos come from SthSthV2 while antonyms come from PAXION, so evaluation is not strictly out-of-domain.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Post-collection manipulations include converting source annotations into multiple-choice QA, randomly sampling 3 to 5 answer options, shuffling option order, randomly shifting start or end points of STAR clips to increase difficulty, and using an LLM to make option lengths similar.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos and annotations are filtered before inclusion: the authors select 11 datasets for diversity, remove short clips and extremely long videos, primarily keep videos ranging from 5s to 35s, and apply task-specific filters such as duration constraints, question-content filters, and program-length limits for source datasets like STAR and CLEVRER.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating the temporal perception and cognition capabilities of multi-modal large language models on open-world video understanding tasks.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: ChatGPT is used to automatically generate questions and, for some tasks, multiple-choice answer options; LLMs are also used to ensure answer options have similar and reasonable lengths. UMT-L/16 is used to provide top-6 action predictions for candidate answers in the Fine-grained Action task.
